hero.headline: Airlines Face $100 Billion Fuel Cost Increase as Iran Conflict Disrupts Energy Markets
hero.body:
The global airline industry is bracing for an additional $100 billion in jet fuel expenses this year following the conflict in Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping channel for crude oil. The surge in fuel costs has forced carriers to slash profit forecasts and acknowledge that higher ticket prices are unavoidable.

Industry leaders gathered in Rio de Janeiro for the International Air Transport Association's 82nd Annual General Meeting to discuss the financial fallout. With jet fuel prices expected to be 70 percent higher across 2026, collective industry profits worldwide are projected to halve to $23 billion. IATA Director General Willie Walsh stated: "High oil prices will inevitably mean higher ticket prices. There's just no way to avoid that."

Jet fuel represents one of the largest variable costs for airlines, making the price surge particularly damaging to operating margins. While OPEC Plus announced plans to increase output by 188,000 barrels per day, this move offers limited relief given the massive quantities of oil prevented from reaching markets by the Strait of Hormuz closure.

For some carriers, the fuel price shock poses an existential threat. Walsh described the situation as "potentially existential" for many airlines, characterizing it as "a challenging and unpredictable time" with "wafer-thin margins." However, he noted that concerns about actual fuel shortages have diminished, and the industry remains profitable with traffic up 2 percent.

The timing of this crisis complicates an industry still stabilizing after pandemic-related disruptions. Walsh observed that "if you factor out the impact on the Middle East for the rest of the world it remains a pretty positive environment," with expectations for a strong northern summer season.

Fare increases will likely hit certain passenger categories hardest. Sean Doyle, chief executive of British Airways, suggested that long-haul and business passengers would absorb the bulk of price increases, while price-sensitive short-haul holiday flights would face smaller hikes. "If fuel goes up, fares have to go up," Doyle said.

Research from IATA indicates that roughly half of passengers are prepared to spend substantially more on fares if prices track oil costs. This willingness may help offset some impact during peak travel seasons.

Beyond fuel concerns, European airlines face additional headwinds from new border regulations. The EU's entry-exit system, scheduled for full implementation by September 7, will require biometric checks on most non-EU citizens. IATA warned that processing times could extend from 20 to 25 seconds to 90 seconds per passenger, creating significant congestion at European airports during peak travel periods. Rafael Schvartsman, IATA's vice president for Europe, cautioned that "the probability that people will be waiting in lines for a long time is very, very high," particularly affecting major Mediterranean destinations.

cards.headline: Israel reports Iranian missile launch during fragile ceasefire
cards.teaser: The attack would mark the first since a ceasefire took effect in early April.
cards.body:
Israel reported that Iran launched a missile at Israeli territory, marking the first such attack since a fragile ceasefire began in early April. The strike threatens to undermine ongoing mediation efforts aimed at reaching a permanent agreement to end the conflict.

The reported Iranian missile launch represents a significant escalation during the pause in hostilities. Mediators have been working to negotiate a deal that would resolve the broader war.

cards.headline: Trump says he will urge Netanyahu not to retaliate against Iran
cards.teaser: The president told Axios he plans to call the Israeli prime minister to press against further strikes following Iran's missile attack.
cards.body:
President Trump said he will call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to urge him not to retaliate for Iran's missile attack. Trump told Axios that both countries have struck and further escalation is unnecessary.

Trump stated he would tell Netanyahu that Israel and Iran each had their strike and no additional response is needed. The ceasefire in the Middle East faces strain after Israel struck Beirut and Iran responded with multiple waves of missiles. Trump is working to prevent escalations that could undermine prospects for a lasting peace agreement.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus to Increase Oil Output as Strait of Hormuz Remains Closed
cards.teaser: The cartel will boost production by 188,000 barrels per day despite the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus announced plans to increase oil production by 188,000 barrels per day as efforts to secure a ceasefire in Iran continue without success. The move comes as the conflict disrupts global energy markets.

The production increase is largely symbolic given the vast amounts of oil stranded by the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz. The strait serves as a critical passage for oil transport, and its closure prevents normal movement of crude from major producing regions regardless of output levels.

cards.headline: Zelensky Meets European Leaders in London as US Steps Back From Mediation
cards.teaser: Ukraine's president traveled to Britain to meet with leaders from Germany, France, and the UK as Washington reduces its role in peace negotiations.
cards.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany, and France at Downing Street on Sunday to discuss Ukraine's path forward. The gathering of Ukraine's closest European allies comes as U.S. President Donald Trump's diplomatic focus has shifted toward the conflict with Iran, reducing American involvement in peace mediation efforts.

Zelensky indicated that European leaders could take on a larger negotiating role in potential discussions with Russia. The shift reflects changing dynamics in efforts to resolve the Ukraine war, with European nations stepping into a more prominent position as mediators.

cards.headline: Israel launches strikes on Beirut suburbs in response to Hezbollah attack
cards.teaser: The retaliatory attack followed a Hezbollah strike on Israeli military positions using fighter drones.
cards.body:
Israel struck suburbs of Beirut in a retaliatory operation against Hezbollah, according to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office. The strikes followed a Hezbollah attack on Israeli military positions using fighter drones.

The exchange marks the latest escalation in the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militant group.

cards.headline: Senate passes immigration enforcement funding bill
cards.body:
Senate Democrats have blocked a funding package for the Department of Homeland Security, pushing the agency toward a partial shutdown at midnight Friday. The vote fell short of the 60 votes needed to overcome a filibuster, with senators splitting largely along party lines at 52-47 in favor of continuing the department's funding.

The blockade reflects Democratic anger over the Trump administration's immigration enforcement operations and recent deaths in Minneapolis. Last month, federal agents shot and killed two US citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, in the city. The controversy intensified when Tom Homan, the Trump administration's border czar, announced that ICE was largely withdrawing its operations from Minneapolis.

Democrats have demanded significant reforms to how ICE operates before agreeing to fund the agency. Their proposed changes include requiring agents to wear identification and body cameras, and prohibiting enforcement activities near schools, medical facilities, churches, polling stations, childcare facilities and courts. Democrats also want local and state law enforcement to have guaranteed authority to investigate potential crimes by federal agents, including excessive use of force.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said the party was seeking common-sense changes. "From day one, I've said unless there were really strong, meaningful reforms to rein in ICE and stop the violence, there will not be Democratic votes to fund ICE," he said. "We've been pushing commonsense reforms, the very types of things that local police and sheriffs throughout America routinely follow. Today's strong vote was a shot across the bow to Republicans. Democrats will not support a blank check for chaos."

Republicans support body cameras but have resisted other proposals, arguing they would restrict agents' operations. Republican Senator James Lankford of Oklahoma criticized Democrats' approach, saying their reaction to the Minneapolis incident would harm broader homeland security efforts including the Coast Guard, Secret Service, and FEMA.

The shutdown's impact may be limited. ICE and Customs and Border Protection received 75 billion dollars in funding last year through what the Trump administration called a flagship spending bill. This means immigration enforcement agencies will continue operating even if the general DHS funding lapses. Instead, the shutdown would primarily affect agencies like the Transportation Safety Administration, FEMA, and the US Coast Guard.

Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire noted that the department has substantial funding available regardless. "Even if the current funding bill stalls or is not passed that would fund the Department of Homeland Security, the department has an extraordinary amount of money at its disposal right now because it was funded during the big tax bill that my Republican colleagues passed last summer," she said.

The House will now decide whether to take further action on the legislation.

hero.headline: Zelensky Meets European Leaders in London as US Steps Back From Mediation
hero.teaser: Ukraine's president traveled to Britain to meet with leaders from Germany, France, and the UK as Washington reduces its role in peace negotiations.
hero.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany, and France at Downing Street on Sunday to discuss Ukraine's path forward. The gathering of Ukraine's closest European allies comes as U.S. President Donald Trump's diplomatic focus has shifted toward the conflict with Iran, reducing American involvement in peace mediation efforts.

Zelensky indicated that European leaders could take on a larger negotiating role in potential discussions with Russia. The shift reflects changing dynamics in efforts to resolve the Ukraine war, with European nations stepping into a more prominent position as mediators.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Beirut Suburbs Days After US-Brokered Truce
cards.teaser: Israeli forces attacked areas on the outskirts of Lebanon's capital in response to Hezbollah firing at Israeli territory.
cards.body:
Israel conducted airstrikes on Beirut's suburbs on Sunday, days after a U.S.-brokered truce was meant to take effect. The Israeli military said it launched the strikes in response to Hezbollah firing at Israeli territory. According to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office, the attacks followed Hezbollah's use of fighter drones against Israeli military targets.

The exchange of fire indicates that American efforts to establish a lasting cease-fire in Lebanon have faltered. The renewed fighting between Israel and the Iranian-backed militant group undermines the fragile truce arrangements that Washington had recently negotiated.

cards.headline: Gunman Kills One in Attack in Central Israel
cards.teaser: An Arab citizen of Israel carried out a shooting attack before being killed by security forces.
cards.body:
A gunman killed one person in a shooting attack in central Israel on Sunday. Israeli authorities killed the assailant, who was identified as an Arab citizen of Israel.

Hamas, the Palestinian militant group, praised the shooting but did not claim responsibility for the attack. The incident reflects ongoing security tensions in Israel amid escalating regional confrontations.

cards.headline: Peru Holds Presidential Runoff in Test of Regional Political Shift
cards.teaser: Voters cast ballots in a tight race seen as an indicator of Latin America's broader political direction.
cards.body:
Peru held a presidential runoff election on Sunday as voters grappled with rising crime, corruption scandals, and chronic political instability. The country has cycled through nine presidents in a decade, leaving many Peruvians searching for stability and solutions to inequality and insecurity.

The race pitted Keiko Fujimori, a rightwing candidate and daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, against Roberto Sánchez, a leftist congressman and former trade and tourism minister. Fujimori secured 17% in the first round, while Sánchez took 12%, setting up a polarized left-right contest that mirrors Peru's 2021 election dynamics.

cards.headline: Neo-Nazi Party Member Loses Close Mayoral Race in German Town
cards.teaser: A far-right candidate's strong showing in a runoff election signals shifting attitudes toward extremist politics in Germany.
cards.body:
A member of a neo-Nazi party lost a close mayoral race in a German town on Sunday, but his relative success highlighted growing acceptance of far-right politics in the country. Despite the loss in the runoff, the candidate's performance marked a shift in German political norms.

The result caps a growing realization in Germany that voting for the far right, even within living memory of Adolf Hitler, is no longer considered taboo by significant portions of the electorate. The close race has raised concerns among mainstream political leaders about the normalization of extremist political movements.

cards.headline: Trump Ends NBC Interview After Dispute Over Election Claims
cards.teaser: The president cut short a television interview after being challenged on his statements about the 2024 election.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump ended an NBC interview on Sunday after clashing with presenter Kristen Welker over his claims that the election was rigged. Welker repeatedly challenged Trump on multiple points throughout the discussion.

The confrontation underscores the tensions between Trump and major news organizations regarding coverage of his presidency and political statements.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Faces Criticism Over D-Day Immigration Remarks
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth drew condemnation for comments linking European migration policy to the World War II anniversary.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faced widespread criticism on Sunday for remarks about immigration during a D-Day commemoration speech. Hegseth criticized Europe over what he called a migration invasion, drawing condemnation from commentators and at least one House Republican who called the remarks inappropriate.

Residents of a French village said Hegseth was not welcome for a D-Day visit. Hegseth brought six of his children to France on the official trip, according to reports. The comments sparked backlash for what critics called a misuse of a solemn military anniversary to advance political arguments.

hero.headline: 3.6 magnitude earthquake strikes East Bay, followed by smaller aftershock
hero.body:
A 3.6 magnitude earthquake shook the East Bay area near Alamo on Sunday morning, according to the United States Geological Survey. The tremor was followed by a smaller aftershock in the same region. The earthquake affected the San Francisco Bay Area, though the extent of any damage or injuries has not been reported.

The USGS recorded the initial quake, which residents across the East Bay felt. The smaller secondary tremor occurred shortly after the main event. Earthquakes of this magnitude are considered light to moderate and can be felt by people indoors, particularly on upper floors of buildings.

California sits on multiple fault lines and experiences thousands of earthquakes each year, though most are too small to be felt. The East Bay region has experienced notable seismic activity throughout its history, as it lies near the Hayward Fault, one of the most dangerous fault lines in the state. Scientists have long warned that the Bay Area faces significant earthquake risk.

The San Francisco Bay Area is home to millions of residents across multiple counties. Local authorities regularly conduct earthquake preparedness drills and maintain emergency response plans for seismic events. California building codes require structures to meet earthquake safety standards, though older buildings may be more vulnerable to damage.

The USGS monitors seismic activity across the United States and provides real-time data on earthquakes through its monitoring systems. When earthquakes occur, the agency quickly determines their magnitude, location, and depth, then disseminates information to emergency responders and the public. Sunday's earthquake adds to the ongoing seismic activity that characterizes life in earthquake-prone regions of California.

cards.headline: President Trump ends NBC interview after dispute over election claims
cards.teaser: The president walked out of the taping after being challenged by the host on multiple points during the conversation.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump abruptly ended an interview with NBC News host Kristen Welker on "Meet the Press" following a clash over his claims about the election being rigged. Welker repeatedly challenged the president on multiple points during the taping.

Rather than continue the confrontation with the NBC host, Trump chose to walk out of the interview.

cards.headline: Democrats in Congress navigate concerns over Platner allegations
cards.teaser: Party members are grappling with how to respond to allegations involving Senate candidate Graham Platner.
cards.body:
Congressional Democrats are addressing concerns about allegations involving Graham Platner as he pursues a Senate seat. Representative Ro Khanna said he supports Platner's Senate bid despite what he called shameful actions. Maine Democrats remain divided over Platner, with some backing him reluctantly.

The Atlantic reported that the Platner campaign has issued what it described as a calm message amid the scrutiny. The Wall Street Journal examined Platner's rise in politics as the situation continues to develop within the Democratic Party.

cards.headline: Israel launches strikes on Beirut suburbs in response to Hezbollah attack
cards.teaser: The retaliatory attack followed a Hezbollah strike on Israeli military positions using fighter drones.
cards.body:
Israel struck suburbs of Beirut in a retaliatory operation against Hezbollah, according to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office. The strikes followed a Hezbollah attack on Israeli military positions using fighter drones.

The exchange marks the latest escalation in the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militant group.

cards.headline: Israel reports Iranian missile launch during fragile ceasefire
cards.teaser: The attack would mark the first since a ceasefire took effect in early April.
cards.body:
Israel reported that Iran launched a missile at Israeli territory, marking the first such attack since a fragile ceasefire began in early April. The strike threatens to undermine ongoing mediation efforts aimed at reaching a permanent agreement to end the conflict.

The reported Iranian missile launch represents a significant escalation during the pause in hostilities. Mediators have been working to negotiate a deal that would resolve the broader war.

cards.headline: Zelensky meets European leaders in London for Ukraine war discussions
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president held talks at Downing Street with some of Ukraine's strongest European supporters.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with European leaders at Downing Street to discuss the ongoing war in Ukraine. The gathering brought together Ukraine's closest European allies to address the conflict.

The timing of these talks coincides with a shift in US foreign policy priorities. President Donald Trump's attention has turned toward the conflict with Iran, marking a change in the focus of American diplomatic efforts away from the Ukraine war.

cards.headline: Teen dies after heat-related illness on Grand Canyon hike
cards.teaser: An 18-year-old hiker died after showing symptoms of heat distress on the Bright Angel Trail.
cards.body:
An 18-year-old hiker died at Grand Canyon National Park after experiencing heat-related illness during a strenuous hike on the Bright Angel Trail. Park officials responded to a heat distress call on the trail.

Summer temperatures at the Grand Canyon can reach extreme levels, creating dangerous conditions for hikers on challenging trails like the Bright Angel.

cards.headline: Trump Calls for Fed Rate Cut Ahead of New Chairman's First Meeting
cards.teaser: The president pressed the Federal Reserve to avoid raising interest rates following a strong jobs report.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump publicly urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates as Kevin Warsh prepares to take over as chairman. Trump said there was no justification for raising rates following the latest jobs report and warned that an increase would be a mistake.

The strong jobs data surprised markets and triggered a stock sell-off. Barclays analysts cautioned that markets are entering a warning zone as the Fed's monetary policy calculations grow more complicated.

cards.headline: S&P 500 Loses $1.4 Trillion in Market Value After Strong Jobs Report
cards.teaser: Stock markets dropped sharply following employment data that exceeded expectations.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 declined 2.6% following the release of May employment data showing 172,000 jobs added and an unemployment rate holding at 4.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index was hit harder, falling 4% in its largest single-day drop in over a year, while the Dow dropped 1.3%.

The sharp market selloff reflected investor concerns that strong labor market resilience could prompt the Federal Reserve to maintain higher interest rates longer than expected. This prospect pressured stock valuations, particularly in the technology sector.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly's Triple-Action Diabetes Drug Shows Strong Results in Weight Loss and Sleep Apnea
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical company's next-generation obesity medication demonstrated benefits beyond blood sugar control.
cards.body:
Eli Lilly's retatrutide demonstrated significant benefits in a phase 3 trial, with patients losing more than four times as much weight as those receiving a placebo over 40 weeks. Blood sugar control also improved substantially, with average HbA1c reductions more than double those of the placebo group.

The weekly injection works differently than existing diabetes medications. While drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy primarily suppress appetite through the GLP-1 pathway, and Mounjaro combines GLP-1 and GIP, retatrutide targets three mechanisms: it mimics GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon. This triple action controls appetite and blood sugar while also increasing energy expenditure, offering a distinct approach to metabolic disease treatment.

cards.headline: Broadcom CEO Addresses AI and Software Strategy Amid Stock Decline
cards.teaser: The semiconductor company's chief executive delivered unexpected comments on artificial intelligence as shares fell 20 percent.
cards.body:
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan issued remarks on the company's AI and software positioning as the stock experienced a significant downturn. Shares had declined 20 percent, prompting questions about whether the dip represents a buying opportunity.

Analysts offered differing views on the company's prospects, with some seeing potential for 50 percent upside while others characterized Broadcom as a canary in the AI coal mine. The CEO's comments came as investors reassess valuations across the artificial intelligence sector.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Reboot Takes in $55 Million in Biggest R-Rated Comedy Opening in 12 Years
cards.teaser: The film topped the box office with the largest opening weekend for an adult comedy in over a decade.
cards.body:
'Scary Movie' Returns Politically Incorrect Humor to Top of the Box Office

The latest Scary Movie installment earned $55 million over the opening weekend in the United States and Canada, marking the biggest opening for an R-rated comedy in 12 years. The film's politically incorrect humor found an audience in theaters.

The strong performance reflects continued viewer interest in theatrical comedy releases, a genre that has struggled to draw large crowds in recent years. The result demonstrates that audiences remain willing to venture to cinemas for comedy films.

hero.headline: Sega announces Crazy Taxi World Tour reboot using generative AI
hero.body:
Sega officially announced Crazy Taxi World Tour, a reboot of its racing franchise set to launch in 2027, but immediately sparked controversy by confirming the game used generative AI during development. The announcement came during the Xbox Games Showcase, marking the series' return after a two-decade absence from major releases.

The confirmation of generative AI use in the game's development prompted immediate backlash from the gaming community. Sega responded to the criticism, though specific details about which aspects of the game incorporated AI-generated content were not provided in the initial announcement. The controversy overshadowed what was intended as a celebratory reveal of the franchise's comeback.

The original Crazy Taxi became a cultural phenomenon in arcades and on Dreamcast in the late 1990s and early 2000s, known for its high-speed gameplay and punk rock soundtrack. The series has remained largely dormant as a mainline franchise since the mid-2000s, with only occasional mobile releases and ports of earlier games keeping the brand alive.

The use of generative AI in game development has become an increasingly contentious issue in the industry. Many artists, voice actors, and developers have raised concerns about AI tools potentially replacing human creative work and being trained on copyrighted material without permission. Several major game companies have faced similar backlash when announcing AI implementation in their titles.

Crazy Taxi World Tour represents Sega's attempt to revive one of its classic franchises for modern platforms. The game's 2027 release date gives the company time to address community concerns about the AI implementation, though Sega has already issued responses defending its use of the technology in the development process.

cards.headline: Atlantic cold blob linked to weakening ocean current system approaching tipping point
cards.teaser: A mysterious cold patch in the Atlantic Ocean has been traced to a weakening current system that may be nearing a critical threshold.
cards.body:
Scientists analyzing the Atlantic cold blob have concluded the phenomenon results from a weakening Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, a current system that includes the Gulf Stream. The reanalysis suggests the system may be approaching a tipping point that could trigger significant climate consequences.

Researchers argue the potential collapse of the AMOC should be treated as a European security policy matter given its far-reaching impacts. The weakening current system has created an unusual cold patch in the Atlantic that stands in contrast to warming trends elsewhere in the ocean, serving as a visible indicator of the circulation changes underway.

cards.headline: Notion restores Anthropic access after service disruption
cards.teaser: Notion's integration with Anthropic's AI services has been restored following a temporary outage.
cards.body:
Notion announced it had restored access to Anthropic after experiencing a service disruption affecting users relying on the AI integration. The head of product at Notion expressed surprise at the volume of attention the outage received on social media.

The disruption affected users who had incorporated Anthropic's AI capabilities into their Notion workflows. Anthropic provides large language model services that Notion has integrated into its productivity platform, allowing users to leverage AI features within their documents and databases.

cards.headline: Microsoft reveals translucent green Xbox for 25th anniversary
cards.teaser: Microsoft unveiled a limited edition Xbox Series X in translucent green to mark the console brand's 25th anniversary.
cards.body:
Microsoft is celebrating 25 years of Xbox with a special edition console. The Xbox Series X features a translucent green design that draws inspiration from the original Xbox, showcasing the internal components through the see-through casing. The matching controller shares the same transparent green aesthetic.

This marks the first time Microsoft has introduced a translucent design to the Xbox Series X, bringing back a nostalgic design element from gaming's past.

cards.headline: Persona 6 announced for PlayStation 5, Xbox and PC
cards.teaser: Atlus officially announced Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase, confirming the next mainline entry in the role-playing game series.
cards.body:
Atlus officially confirmed Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase 2026, ending years of speculation about the next mainline entry in the series. The game is headed to PlayStation 5, Xbox Series consoles, and PC.

The announcement was brief, offering little beyond confirmation of the game's existence and platform availability. Further details about Persona 6 are expected to be revealed at a later date.

cards.headline: Fable releases in late February with Hayley Atwell as villain
cards.teaser: Microsoft set a late February 2027 release date for Fable and revealed Marvel actor Hayley Atwell voices the game's antagonist.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced that the rebooted Fable will launch on February 23rd, 2027, following a recent delay that pushed the game out of 2026. The company revealed the release date during its Xbox Games Showcase on Sunday, alongside fresh gameplay footage.

Hayley Atwell will voice the game's villain, Isabel Hero of Wraithmarsh. Fable marks the franchise's return since 2010's Fable III, making it a significant release for Xbox's upcoming lineup.

cards.headline: Halo: Campaign Evolved launches July 28 with new space combat
cards.teaser: Microsoft set a July 28 release date for Halo: Campaign Evolved and revealed the game will include new space combat missions.
cards.body:
Microsoft revealed Halo: Campaign Evolved during its Xbox Games Showcase, confirming a July 28 launch across Xbox Series S/X, PC, and PlayStation 5. The remake of Halo: Combat Evolved's campaign includes new content, with a mission trailer showcasing Operation: Meteorite, a three-mission sequence.

Pre-orders are now available for the game ahead of its release next month.

hero.headline: Alexander Zverev wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in a tense five-set final. The second-seeded German player finally secured the major championship that had eluded him throughout his career, despite previous success at every other level of professional tennis.

Zverev had previously won Masters 1000 events, claimed the ATP Finals twice, and earned an Olympic gold medal in Tokyo 2020, but he had lost in all three of his previous Grand Slam finals. The French Open final represented his fourth major final appearance and his first victory at this stage.

The match was marked by considerable tension and nerves on both sides of the net. Zverev dominated the opening set 6-1, but Cobolli fought back to win the second set 6-4 as the German's familiar problems with his forehand and second serve resurfaced. Zverev regained control in the third set with a 6-4 victory, completely outserving his opponent throughout the set. Cobolli crumbled under pressure in the set's final moments, spraying three wild unforced errors.

However, Zverev's nerves intensified as the finish line approached. In the fourth set, he appeared overwhelmed by the moment, though Cobolli also struggled. The set went to a tiebreaker where Cobolli, serving at 5-4 with just 39 percent first-serve success, mounted a brilliant comeback. The Italian saved the championship with a searing running forehand winner to force a fifth set.

In the decisive final set, Cobolli's energy reserves were exhausted. He immediately surrendered his opening service game and never recovered, allowing Zverev to pull away convincingly with a 6-1 victory.

After Cobolli missed an overhead on the second championship point, Zverev dropped to his back and began sobbing. He later addressed his team, saying: "We've been through injuries. We've been through heartbreak. We've been through losses. We've been losers at times in the important moments. But at the end of the day, we're grand slam champions now and that's what counts."

Zverev's path to the final was significantly aided by the absence of top competitors. Top seed Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic were eliminated in consecutive days, while Carlos Alcaraz was absent due to injury. Cobolli, the world number 14, reached his first Grand Slam final without playing in the semifinal after his Italian compatriot Matteo Arnaldi withdrew due to illness.

Speaking after his victory, Zverev reflected on his complex relationship with Roland Garros. "This court is so special to me in so many ways," he said. "I've had the best moments of my life on this court, I had the worst moment of my life on this court. I was laying in that corner over there with seven broken ligaments and two fractured bones. I lost a grand slam final here two years ago. But now, finally, it's a happy end."

cards.headline: Stacey King, three-time NBA champion with Bulls, dies at 59
cards.teaser: The former Bulls player and broadcaster won three championships with Chicago and later became a fan favorite on the team's broadcast crew.
cards.body:
Stacey King, a three-time NBA champion with the Chicago Bulls, has died at 59. King was part of the Bulls' championship teams in the early 1990s alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen.

Following his playing career, King transitioned to broadcasting and became a fan favorite on the Bulls' broadcast team, bringing enthusiasm and basketball knowledge to their telecasts.

cards.headline: Christian Eriksen collapses during Denmark friendly, match called off
cards.teaser: The Danish midfielder collapsed on the pitch during a friendly against Ukraine, with officials confirming he regained consciousness after the incident.
cards.body:
Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during a friendly match against Ukraine on Sunday. Medical personnel immediately attended to him on the field in Odense, and the referee abandoned the match shortly after the incident.

The Danish Football Association confirmed that Eriksen was conscious following the medical emergency. This marks a significant moment for the player, who suffered cardiac arrest during a European Championship match in 2021.

cards.headline: 76ers promote Jameer Nelson to executive vice president
cards.teaser: The former NBA All-Star moves up from assistant general manager to become the No. 2 executive under new president Mike Gansey.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers have promoted assistant general manager Jameer Nelson to executive vice president of basketball operations. The move makes Nelson the franchise's second-ranking executive, working under newly appointed president Mike Gansey.

Nelson, a former NBA All-Star, takes on an expanded role in the 76ers' front office as the organization restructures its leadership.

cards.headline: Tyrrell Hatton wins LIV Golf Andalucia by two shots
cards.teaser: The English golfer shot one-under par 70 in the final round to secure victory at the LIV Golf event in Spain.
cards.body:
Tyrrell Hatton of England won the LIV Golf Andalucia tournament, carding a final-round 70 to finish two shots ahead of the field. The victory continues Hatton's success on the LIV Golf circuit since joining the breakaway tour.

Hatton's one-under par performance in the final round was steady enough to hold off his competitors and secure the title. The win adds to his resume on the LIV tour and provides momentum heading into upcoming events on the schedule.

cards.headline: Tigers ace Tarik Skubal pitches five scoreless innings in rehab start
cards.teaser: The left-hander made his first minor league appearance since elbow surgery last month, showing progress in his recovery.
cards.body:
Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal completed his first minor league rehabilitation appearance following elbow surgery, pitching five scoreless innings. The outing represents a significant milestone in his recovery process as he works toward rejoining the major league roster.

Skubal underwent the elbow procedure last month and has been out of action since then. The successful rehab start indicates his recovery is moving forward as the team continues to manage his workload during his return to game action.

cards.headline: Hurricanes coach noncommittal on Game 4 lineup changes
cards.teaser: Rod Brind'Amour said he does not anticipate major adjustments after Carolina fell behind 2-1 in the Stanley Cup Final against Vegas.
cards.body:
Carolina Hurricanes coach Rod Brind'Amour indicated he does not expect to make significant changes to his lineup for Game 4 of the Stanley Cup Final. The Hurricanes trail the Vegas Golden Knights 2-1 in the series after dropping the previous game.

Brind'Amour declined to specify whether he would make a goaltending change or adjust his skater combinations. The coach's comments suggest he maintains confidence in the current roster despite the series deficit heading into a must-win situation.

hero.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Marry in Sicily Ceremony
hero.body:
Singer Dua Lipa and British actor Callum Turner have married, with celebrations taking place in Sicily and featuring a performance by Elton John. The couple first met in 2023 after being introduced at the River Cafe in west London, though they did not begin dating until a year later when they reconnected at a restaurant in Los Angeles. Turner, 36, is an actor who has been widely mentioned as a potential candidate for the next James Bond role.

The couple became engaged weeks before a holiday to Palermo last July, where they shared photos of themselves exploring the Sicilian capital. Images posted on Instagram showed them walking through baroque streets, visiting the cathedral, and enjoying sunset boat trips. Their affection for the city was evident, with one photo capturing the word "amore" written on a wall. During their visit, they stopped at Colletti, a bar in the city centre, where the owner Alessandro Minnone described Lupa as "very down-to-earth and warm."

Plans for a Palermo wedding had circulated for months. Local media reported that a wedding planner had been hired to arrange celebrations in the city, with reports suggesting that rooms at Villa Igiea, a five-star art nouveau hotel, were reserved for guests. However, a source at the hotel confirmed that while guest rooms had been booked, the ceremony itself would not take place there. Different venues had been speculated as possible locations for the ceremony, including the inner courtyard of Palermo's gallery for modern art and the restored church of Santa Maria dello Spasimo.

Lupa's connection to Palermo extends beyond her relationship with Turner. In 2023, she appeared in promotional images wearing the pink shirt of Palermo football club to promote Puma trainers, which the club shared on social media with enthusiasm. The prospect of her wedding in the city generated significant excitement among local residents, who saw it as recognition of Palermo's growing status as a destination for high-profile celebrations.

The wedding news comes at a time when destination weddings in Sicily have become increasingly popular among celebrities and wealthy figures. The island offers both privacy and scenic settings for celebrations. Lupa, 30, is a Grammy-winning singer known for her successful music career, while Turner has appeared in various film and television projects.

The couple's decision to marry in Sicily reflects broader trends in celebrity wedding planning, with Italy emerging as a preferred location for significant life events. Their Sicilian celebration, featuring the musical talents of Elton John, added considerable star power to an already notable entertainment industry event, drawing coverage from multiple outlets.

cards.headline: Nithya Raman Narrows Gap in Los Angeles Mayoral Race
cards.teaser: Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman is closing in on Spencer Pratt in the race for mayor and is expected to overtake him for second place.
cards.body:
Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman is within striking distance of Spencer Pratt in the race for the city's next mayor. She is expected to overtake the Republican and former reality star for second place when the next round of ballot tallies is released.

Raman was previously slotted in a distant position but has gained ground as vote counting continues. Pratt, known for his appearances on reality television, has expressed frustration with the slow pace of vote counting in the ongoing election.

cards.headline: Bob Dylan Performs Basement Tapes Song for First Time in 14 Years
cards.teaser: Bob Dylan performed "You Ain't Goin' Nowhere" during a recent concert, marking the first time he has played the song in 14 years.
cards.body:
Bob Dylan performed the Basement Tapes song "You Ain't Goin' Nowhere" during a recent concert, marking the first time the artist has played the track in 14 years. The performance came two days after Dylan performed another Basement Tapes rarity, "Baby, Won't You Be My Baby," for the first time since recording it 59 years ago.

The Basement Tapes songs were recorded decades ago and have rarely appeared in Dylan's live performances. The back-to-back performances of these deep catalog tracks represent an unusual choice in Dylan's setlist selections during his current tour.

cards.headline: New Spyro Game Announced for Spring 2027 Release
cards.teaser: The first new Spyro game in nearly two decades will release next spring, featuring the franchise's first dragon-flight feature.
cards.body:
Toys for Bob is developing the first original Spyro game in nearly two decades, titled "Spyro: Realms Beyond." The purple dragon returns with his iconic quiff design and will be voiced by Tom Kenny, who originated the character. The game launches in spring 2027 across Xbox, PlayStation 5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2.

A major new feature allows players to take flight at any time during gameplay. Creative director Lou Studdert emphasized the freedom this provides, explaining that players can dive to build speed, use fire-breath to create updrafts, and flap their wings strategically. The redesigned adventure aims to fully explore what it means to play as a dragon.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Opens Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland
cards.teaser: Ariana Grande performed the opening show of her Eternal Sunshine Tour at Oakland Arena.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande launched her Eternal Sunshine Tour with an opening performance at Oakland Arena on Saturday night. The concert demonstrated her vocal prowess and commanding stage presence, delivering what critics characterized as a strong start to the tour.

The show highlighted Grande's multifaceted talents as a performer, setting the tone for the remainder of her tour supporting the Eternal Sunshine album.

cards.headline: Vincent Cassel to Play Napoleon in Video Game Valor Mortis
cards.teaser: Vincent Cassel will play Napoleon Bonaparte in the upcoming first-person video game Valor Mortis.
cards.body:
Vincent Cassel, who will star in the fourth season of HBO's "The White Lotus," is set to play Napoleon Bonaparte in the upcoming first-person video game "Valor Mortis." The game is described as a Soulslike title set in a supernatural reimagining of 19th-century Europe.

Players will take on the role of William, a resurrected soldier of the Grande Armée, according to the game's description. The casting adds a notable film actor to a video game project that blends historical and supernatural elements.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Addresses Pittsburgh Concert Cancellation
cards.teaser: Morgan Wallen responded to criticism over his canceled Pittsburgh show, citing safety concerns about his stage setup in adverse weather conditions.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled his Pittsburgh concert scheduled for Saturday at Acrisure Stadium due to adverse weather forecasts. However, the severe weather that prompted the decision did not ultimately occur, sparking speculation among fans about the real reason for the cancellation.

Wallen addressed the controversy directly, explaining that his large stage setup posed a safety risk during severe weather conditions. He emphasized that protecting concertgoers and crew members from potential danger was worth canceling the show, dismissing what he called "a lot of nonsense" surrounding the decision.

hero.headline: Senate passes immigration enforcement funding bill
hero.body:
Senate Democrats have blocked a funding package for the Department of Homeland Security, pushing the agency toward a partial shutdown at midnight Friday. The vote fell short of the 60 votes needed to overcome a filibuster, with senators splitting largely along party lines at 52-47 in favor of continuing the department's funding.

The blockade reflects Democratic anger over the Trump administration's immigration enforcement operations and recent deaths in Minneapolis. Last month, federal agents shot and killed two US citizens, Renee Good and Alex Pretti, in the city. The controversy intensified when Tom Homan, the Trump administration's border czar, announced that ICE was largely withdrawing its operations from Minneapolis.

Democrats have demanded significant reforms to how ICE operates before agreeing to fund the agency. Their proposed changes include requiring agents to wear identification and body cameras, and prohibiting enforcement activities near schools, medical facilities, churches, polling stations, childcare facilities and courts. Democrats also want local and state law enforcement to have guaranteed authority to investigate potential crimes by federal agents, including excessive use of force.

Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said the party was seeking common-sense changes. "From day one, I've said unless there were really strong, meaningful reforms to rein in ICE and stop the violence, there will not be Democratic votes to fund ICE," he said. "We've been pushing commonsense reforms, the very types of things that local police and sheriffs throughout America routinely follow. Today's strong vote was a shot across the bow to Republicans. Democrats will not support a blank check for chaos."

Republicans support body cameras but have resisted other proposals, arguing they would restrict agents' operations. Republican Senator James Lankford of Oklahoma criticized Democrats' approach, saying their reaction to the Minneapolis incident would harm broader homeland security efforts including the Coast Guard, Secret Service, and FEMA.

The shutdown's impact may be limited. ICE and Customs and Border Protection received 75 billion dollars in funding last year through what the Trump administration called a flagship spending bill. This means immigration enforcement agencies will continue operating even if the general DHS funding lapses. Instead, the shutdown would primarily affect agencies like the Transportation Safety Administration, FEMA, and the US Coast Guard.

Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire noted that the department has substantial funding available regardless. "Even if the current funding bill stalls or is not passed that would fund the Department of Homeland Security, the department has an extraordinary amount of money at its disposal right now because it was funded during the big tax bill that my Republican colleagues passed last summer," she said.

The House will now decide whether to take further action on the legislation.

cards.headline: Trump says he will urge Netanyahu not to retaliate against Iran
cards.teaser: The president told Axios he plans to call the Israeli prime minister to press against further strikes following Iran's missile attack.
cards.body:
President Trump said he will call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to urge him not to retaliate for Iran's missile attack. Trump told Axios that both countries have struck and further escalation is unnecessary.

Trump stated he would tell Netanyahu that Israel and Iran each had their strike and no additional response is needed. The ceasefire in the Middle East faces strain after Israel struck Beirut and Iran responded with multiple waves of missiles. Trump is working to prevent escalations that could undermine prospects for a lasting peace agreement.

cards.headline: President Trump discusses Iran negotiations and administration policies in NBC interview
cards.teaser: Trump addressed ongoing talks with Iran and defended a short-lived anti-weaponization fund in a wide-ranging interview.
cards.body:
President Trump sat down with NBC's Kristen Welker for a wide-ranging interview that aired Sunday, marking his approach to the 18-month mark of his second term. The conversation became testy at times, with Welker challenging Trump on multiple topics throughout the discussion.

Trump told Axios he plans to call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to urge him not to retaliate for Iran's recent missile attack. The president also discussed potential deals involving artificial intelligence, suggesting the American people could benefit from the success of AI ventures.

cards.headline: House Intelligence Democrat calls acting intelligence director appointment dangerous
cards.teaser: Rep. Jim Himes labeled Bill Pulte's selection as acting Director of National Intelligence the worst Trump appointment.
cards.body:
Rep. Jim Himes of Connecticut, the ranking member of the House Intelligence Committee, criticized President Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting Director of National Intelligence. Himes called it the worst and most dangerous appointment made by the president.

Pulte currently serves as head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency. Multiple lawmakers from both parties have criticized the appointment. Himes is among several bipartisan members who have expressed opposition to Trump's selection of Pulte for the intelligence role.

cards.headline: Republican congressman criticizes defense secretary's D-Day speech
cards.teaser: Rep. Michael McCaul said Pete Hegseth made inappropriate remarks during the 82nd anniversary commemoration.
cards.body:
Rep. Michael McCaul of Texas criticized Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Sunday for making "inappropriate" remarks during a speech at the 82nd commemoration of D-Day.

McCaul said the event should have focused on honoring the sacrifice and service of the soldiers who fought during the historic invasion.

cards.headline: Lawsuit seeks to block UFC fight at White House
cards.teaser: A Saturday filing challenges the Trump administration's plan to host a UFC event at the White House on June 14.
cards.body:
A federal lawsuit is attempting to halt a UFC event scheduled for the White House South Lawn next week on President Trump's 80th birthday. The event is being presented as part of celebrations marking the nation's 250th anniversary.

The lawsuit alleges the event benefits Trump financially, citing reports that the president purchased tickets to the fight.

cards.headline: Independent Senate candidates make case for nonpartisan approach
cards.teaser: Seth Bodnar and Dan Osborn argued for independence from both major parties in their Senate campaigns.
cards.body:
Two independent Senate candidates advocated for their nonpartisan approach to upper chamber races. Seth Bodnar and Dan Osborn spoke about their campaigns and commitment to independence from both major parties.

Bodnar said he is telling voters in his state that he is running as an independent and will not work for either party. Both candidates emphasized they would work for constituents rather than partisan interests. The two independents are running in solid red states.
